views.name: user_badges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS UserId,
  COALESCE(bc.badge_count, 0) AS badge_count,
  bc.first_awarded_date,
  bc.last_awarded_date
FROM users_core u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    UserId,
    COUNT(*) AS badge_count,
    MIN(Date) AS first_awarded_date,
    MAX(Date) AS last_awarded_date
  FROM badges
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY UserId
) bc ON bc.UserId = u.Id
grain: users.Id  -- one row per user (via UserId)
views.description: Badge counts per user and latest badge date to support user-level reputation/badge analyses and filters.

views.name: user_last_activity_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS UserId,
  -- classify event type: 'post' from posts, 'comment' from comments, 'vote' from votes, 'history' from postHistory, 'badge' from badges
  evt.event_type,
  evt.event_date,
  evt.rn
FROM users u
JOIN (
  SELECT
    OwnerUserId AS UserId,
    'post' AS event_type,
    CreaionDate AS event_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY OwnerUserId ORDER BY COALESCE(CreaionDate, '0000-01-01') DESC) AS rn
  FROM posts
  WHERE OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    UserId,
    'comment' AS event_type,
    CreationDate AS event_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY UserId ORDER BY COALESCE(CreationDate, '0000-01-01') DESC) AS rn
  FROM comments
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    UserId,
    'vote' AS event_type,
    CreationDate AS event_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY UserId ORDER BY COALESCE(CreationDate, '0000-01-01') DESC) AS rn
  FROM votes
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    UserId,
    'history' AS event_type,
    CreationDate AS event_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY UserId ORDER BY COALESCE(CreationDate, '0000-01-01') DESC) AS rn
  FROM postHistory
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    UserId,
    'badge' AS event_type,
    Date AS event_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY UserId ORDER BY COALESCE(Date, '0000-01-01') DESC) AS rn
  FROM badges
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
) AS evt ON evt.UserId = u.Id
views.description: Per-user ranking of related post-history or post events by timestamp to support latest-activity or latest-post queries; exposes latest event date per user as well as rank for ordering.

LEFT JOIN users ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
grain: one row per post-owner relationship (posts.Id + owner user if present)
views.description: Denormalized mapping of posts to their owner user info to simplify queries that need post metadata alongside author profile.

views.name: posts_core_47
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId,
  posts.AcceptedAnswerId AS AcceptedAnswerId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount,
  posts.CommentCount AS CommentCount,
  posts.FavoriteCount AS FavoriteCount
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical row-level representation of posts with key identifying and descriptive columns used for filtering, joining and display. Keeps original post attributes needed by many questions (owner, title, tags, parent/accepted answers, counts and timestamps).

views.name: users_core_48
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  users.LastAccessDate AS LastAccessDate,
  users.Location AS Location,
  users.Views AS Views,
  users.UpVotes AS UpVotes,
  users.DownVotes AS DownVotes,
  users.AccountId AS AccountId
FROM users
views.description: Canonical row-level representation of users exposing identity, reputation and basic profile fields commonly used to identify owners, filter by user or display user attributes.

views.name: posts_with_owner_49
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS post_Id,
  posts.Title AS post_Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS post_OwnerUserId,
  users.DisplayName AS user_DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS user_Reputation,
  posts.CreaionDate AS post_CreationDate
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users
  ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
grain: one row per post (posts.Id) with owner user columns appended
views.description: Denormalized view joining posts to their owner user record. Exposes post fields alongside owner's DisplayName and basic profile fields for easy retrieval of owner information for a given post.

views.name: posts_basic_50
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId
FROM posts
views.description: One-row-per-post canonical projection with key identifiers and common searchable/textual fields normalized for joins and filtering.

views.name: post_history_edits
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  postHistory.Id AS Id,
  postHistory.PostId AS PostId,
  postHistory.PostHistoryTypeId AS PostHistoryTypeId,
  postHistory.UserId AS UserId,
  postHistory.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  postHistory.Text AS Text
FROM postHistory
WHERE postHistory.UserId IS NOT NULL
views.description: Post history rows for posts including the user that made the history entry; useful to identify users who edited or otherwise changed a post. Keeps one row per postHistory.Id.

views.name: comments_by_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.Score AS Score
FROM comments
WHERE comments.UserId IS NOT NULL
views.description: Comments joined with their author id and basic comment metadata; one row per comment. Designed to be filtered by a set of user ids to find comments authored by those users.

views.name: posts_core_53
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  COALESCE(posts.Title, '') AS Title,
  COALESCE(posts.Tags, '') AS Tags,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COALESCE(posts.Score, 0) AS Score,
  COALESCE(posts.ViewCount, 0) AS ViewCount,
  COALESCE(posts.AnswerCount, 0) AS AnswerCount,
  COALESCE(posts.CommentCount, 0) AS CommentCount,
  COALESCE(posts.FavoriteCount, 0) AS FavoriteCount,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId
FROM posts
views.description: Normalized core information about posts (questions and answers) exposing identifiers, title, tags, owner and key counts/metrics. Clean up nullable fields and provide canonical column names for joins.

views.name: users_core_54
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  DisplayName,
  Reputation,
  CreationDate,
  AccountId
FROM users
views.description: Basic user profile information exposing stable user id and display name and common dimensions used for attribution and reporting.

views.name: posts_core_55
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical/clean projection of posts exposing primary identifiers, title, tags and view/owner metadata. Keeps raw numeric measures (ViewCount, Score) and canonical keys for joins.

views.name: post_viewcount_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS PostId,
  AVG(p.ViewCount) AS avg_viewcount,
  MIN(p.ViewCount) AS min_viewcount,
  MAX(p.ViewCount) AS max_viewcount,
  COUNT(p.ViewCount) AS cnt_viewcount_values
FROM posts p
WHERE p.ViewCount IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.Id

semantic_filters.ViewCount: IS NOT NULL  -- exclude NULLs when computing aggregates

views.description: Aggregated viewcount metrics per post. Computes aggregates (AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT of non-null ViewCount) per post.Id without applying higher-level topic/tag filters. Designed for reuse in analyses that need per-post view statistics.

views.name: badges_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  UserId,
  Name,
  Date
FROM badges
WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
views.description: Row-level badge records with original columns, filtered to only include badges tied to a user (UserId not null). Useful as the base cohort of awarded badges.

views.name: badges_per_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  badges.UserId AS UserId,
  COUNT(badges.Id) AS badge_count,
  MIN(badges.Date) AS first_badge_date,
  MAX(badges.Date) AS last_badge_date
FROM badges
WHERE badges.UserId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY badges.UserId
views.description: Aggregated badge counts per user. One row per UserId with the raw count of badge rows and optional earliest/latest award dates. Useful for answering questions about how many badges each user has and temporal badge stats.

views.name: user_posts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.Tags AS Tags
FROM posts
WHERE posts.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per post with canonical owner info. Exposes post fields and the owner user id/display name to build user-level cohorts and to filter on post attributes (views, title, tags).

views.name: post_history_by_post_and_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  PostId,
  UserId,
  COUNT(*) AS history_count
FROM postHistory
GROUP BY PostId, UserId
views.description: Counts of postHistory rows grouped by post and the user who made that history entry. Useful to check how many history entries a given user has for a post.

views.name: badges_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  badges.Id AS Id,
  badges.UserId AS UserId,
  badges.Name AS Name,
  badges.Date AS Date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', badges.Date) AS INTEGER) AS year
FROM badges
views.description: Row-level badge records with canonicalized date-year extraction and essential badge attributes. Keeps one row per badge and exposes fields useful for filtering and aggregation by year, user, and badge name.

views.name: badges_by_name_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Name AS Name,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', Date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  COUNT(Id) AS count_in_year,
  SUM(COUNT(Id)) OVER (PARTITION BY Name) AS total_count_for_name
FROM badges
GROUP BY Name, year
views.description: Aggregated counts of badges grouped by badge name and year. Produces counts per (Name, year) and also a total count per Name across all years (year NULL indicates missing/unknown).

views.name: badge_counts_for_named_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.Name AS Name,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', b.Date) = '2010' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS count_2010,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', b.Date) = '2011' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS count_2011,
  COUNT(b.Id) AS total_count
FROM badges b
GROUP BY b.Name
views.description: Pivot-like view that presents counts for a given badge Name across years as columns (year values kept as column suffixes). Designed to make year-to-year comparisons simpler in downstream queries.

views.name: posts_by_owner_64
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  OwnerUserId,
  PostTypeId,
  CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
views.description: Row-level posts relation keyed by owner user id; includes post id and minimal metadata for filtering/aggregation by owner.

views.name: user_post_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COUNT(p.Id) AS post_count
FROM posts_by_owner p
GROUP BY p.OwnerUserId
views.description: Aggregated per-user post counts computed from posts_by_owner; exposes user id and total posts to support cohort selection by activity.

views.name: votes_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  PostId,
  VoteTypeId,
  datetime(CreationDate) AS CreationDate,
  UserId,
  BountyAmount
FROM votes
WHERE CreationDate IS NOT NULL
views.description: Normalized vote rows with canonical typed CreationDate and essential identifiers. Exposes one row per vote with CreationDate cast to DATETIME and relevant keys for filtering and grouping by year/date.

views.name: votes_by_calendar_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', CreationDate) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  COUNT(*) AS vote_count
FROM votes
WHERE CreationDate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%Y', CreationDate) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Pre-aggregated counts of votes per calendar year. Useful for year-over-year comparisons and ratio calculations. Keeps one row per year with the raw vote_count.

views.name: posts_core_68
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
WHERE posts.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
views.description: Primary posts rows exposing ownership, counts and basic metadata; excludes posts with NULL owner to focus on authored posts.

views.name: posts_by_owner_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COUNT(p.Id) AS post_count,
  MAX(COALESCE(p.AnswerCount, 0)) AS max_answer_count,
  AVG(COALESCE(p.AnswerCount, 0.0)) AS avg_answer_count,
  MAX(COALESCE(p.Score, 0)) AS max_score,
  MIN(p.CreationDate) AS min_creation_date
FROM posts_with_owner p
WHERE p.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.OwnerUserId
views.description: Per-owner aggregated metrics over their posts (e.g., max/min/avg counts) to support top-k and summary queries by user.

views.name: posts_core_70
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId
FROM posts
views.description: One-row-per-post core attributes needed for analytics: owner, view counts, title and identifiers. Null view counts left as-is (caller may treat null as 0).

views.name: users_core_71
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.CreationDate AS CreationDate
FROM users
views.description: One-row-per-user core attributes used for joining to posts and identifying users by display name.

views.name: user_post_views
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS PostId,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS UserId,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount
FROM posts
JOIN users ON users.Id = posts.OwnerUserId
WHERE posts.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
grain: posts.Id (one row per post with owner info)
views.description: Denormalized relation that pairs each post with its owner's user row and exposes the post view count for aggregations. Keeps raw ViewCount (NULLs preserved) and exposes keys for grouping.
